metric: Pairs shown different by a constraint-respecting database on which both queries were run (DuckDB), and pairs on which 600 random databases (400 wider ones when a query has HAVING, and every database of at most 2 rows per table) showed no difference (not a proof, not bounded verification).
correctness: Every refutation was executed on both queries, is stable under row-order shuffles, and returns the same rows with DuckDB's optimizer off; none are claimed without a database
coverage_of: The 40 pairs the prover leaves unknown in verieql-literature-proof (the other 24 of 64 are proved there): refuted, unknown (agree on every database tried) or unsupported (not run).
caveats: Pairs carry no labels; wrongness is checked against VeriEQL's published counterexamples and a second random search. 14 of the 64 pairs differ between our file and VeriEQL's published outcomes file and were not audited. Developed against these pairs (tuned on test). Whole-row predicates (B1(X)) are spelled out over the row's columns; DuckDB runs them as a fixed hashed macro and the prover as uninterpreted functions. In this row 'unknown' counts pairs that agree on every database tried and 'unsupported' counts pairs DuckDB or the parser rejects. Measured on master 80ac740, after the structural aggregate rules (src/kumosql/aggregate_rules.py, #371). Re-measured on master 4d294afd (sqlglot 30.21, z3-solver 5.1.0.0, an otherwise idle 4-core machine): 25 refuted (unchanged), 9 agree (was 13) because 4 more pairs are proved, 2 not run. Whether the gain comes from rules merged since 2026-10-02 or from solver timeouts that no longer fire on an idle machine was not separated.
